findings.title: VMSA-2024-0012: VMware vCenter Server security updates address out-of-bounds write and information disclosure vulnerabilities (CVE-2024-37079, CVE-2024-37080, CVE-2024-37081)
findings.summary_md: Broadcom released VMSA-2024-0012 on June 17, 2024, fixing CVE-2024-37079, an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the implementation of the DCERPC protocol in VMware vCenter Server, alongside CVE-2024-37080 and CVE-2024-37081. NVD cites this notification as the vendor advisory and patch reference. Broadcom's companion FAQ records that the advisory carried no workarounds and that at release VMware was not aware of exploitation in the wild.

findings.title: VMSA-2024-0012: Questions & Answers (vmware/vcf-security-and-compliance-guidelines)
findings.summary_md: Broadcom's official companion FAQ to VMSA-2024-0012, initially published at 2130 PDT on June 17, 2024, confirms the advisory release date and lists CVE-2024-37079, CVE-2024-37080 and CVE-2024-37081. It states there are no workarounds in the advisory, that ESXi hosts are not affected, and that Cloud Foundation receives an asynchronous patch. It also documents a 7.0 U3q/U3r patching failure with custom TLS cipher configurations that aborts the vpxd-svcs service, tracked in KB 369485.

findings.title: NVD record for CVE-2024-37079 (heap overflow in DCERPC implementation)
findings.summary_md: The CVE record, published June 18, 2024 with Broadcom's security team as CNA, describes a heap-overflow vulnerability in the implementation of the DCERPC protocol, triggered by a specially crafted network packet and potentially leading to remote code execution, with a CVSS 3.1 base score of 9.8. Affected versions are vCenter Server below 8.0 U2d, below 8.0 U1e and below 7.0 U3r, plus Cloud Foundation 5.x and 4.x. The record carries CISA's SSVC assessment dated January 23, 2026: exploitation active, automatable yes, technical impact total.

findings.title: CVE-2024-37079: VMware vCenter Server Integer Underflow Code Execution Vulnerability (ZDI)
findings.summary_md: Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative published a full exploitation writeup on August 28, 2024, crediting Hao Zheng and Zibo Li of the TianGong Team of Legendsec at Qi'anxin Group as the original discoverers. The analysis shows an integer underflow triggered by DCERPC Bind or Alter Context requests carrying exactly 169 presentation context elements, hitting the Likewise Open libdcerpc.so used by services on TCP 2014, 2012 and 2020, and supplies a detection rule: flag DCE/RPC packet types 0x0b or 0x0e with auth_len greater than zero and 169 or more context elements. ZDI noted at the time that no attacks had been detected in the wild and that exploitation would not be straightforward.

findings.title: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog entry for CVE-2024-37079
findings.summary_md: CISA added CVE-2024-37079 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on January 23, 2026 with a required-action due date of February 13, 2026, describing the out-of-bounds write in the DCERPC implementation that can lead to remote code execution. The entry's ransomware-campaign-use field is Unknown and forensic triage is not flagged. CISA's associated SSVC decision points on the NVD record mark exploitation active and the vulnerability automatable.
